summary_en: This Phase 1 study is testing ABBV-324, an investigational drug, in adults with hepatocellular cancer or squamous-cell non-small cell lung cancer. ABBV-324 is given by intravenous (IV) infusion, and some participants receive oral lenvatinib; the study lasts about 6.5 years and how often doses are given is not stated. The study measures adverse events and change in disease activity, and it is a Phase 1 study.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa ABBV-324, un medicamento en investigación, en adultos con cáncer hepatocelular o cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas de tipo escamoso. ABBV-324 se administra por infusión intravenosa (IV), algunos participantes reciben lenvatinib oral, el estudio dura unos 6.5 años y la frecuencia de las dosis no se indica. El estudio mide los eventos adversos y el cambio en la actividad de la enfermedad; es un estudio de fase 1.
who_for: Locally advanced, metastatic or unresectable HCC confirmed by histology or cytology; Part 2 requires prior checkpoint inhibitor regimen and no prior lenvatinib.
Part 1 only: advanced LUSC not amenable to surgery, after failure of platinum chemotherapy with an immune checkpoint inhibitor and/or targeted therapy.
not_for: Fibrolamellar HCC, sarcomatoid HCC, or mixed cholangiocarcinoma/HCC.
Unresolved adverse events above Grade 1 from prior anticancer therapy, except alopecia.
Untreated brain or meningeal metastases, or metastases needing ongoing steroids for cerebral edema.
History of interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis needing systemic steroids, or active ILD or pneumonitis on screening CT.
Anticancer therapy stopped within 14 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is shorter) before the first ABBV-324 dose.
